content: Amoxicillin is an antibiotic approved by the FDA for treating infections of the ear, nose, throat, genitourinary tract, and lower respiratory tract. It is also used for gonorrhea and Helicobacter pylori infections. Common side effects include rash, diarrhea, nausea, headache, and vulvovaginitis. Adult Indications and Dosage: 1. Triple Therapy for H. pylori Infection: Amoxicillin 1 gram, clarithromycin 500 mg, and lansoprazole 30 mg, all taken orally twice daily for 14 days. 2. Community-Acquired Pneumonia: For patients with comorbidities or recent antimicrobial use: 875 mg orally every 12 hours or 500 mg every 8 hours. 3. Acute Bacterial Rhinosinusitis: Mild/Moderate: 500 mg every 12 hours or 250 mg every 8 hours. Severe: 875 mg every 12 hours or 500 mg every 8 hours. 4. Gonorrhea (Uncomplicated Anogenital and Urethral Infections): Single oral dose of 3 grams. 5. Skin and Subcutaneous Tissue Infections: Mild/Moderate: 500 mg every 12 hours or 250 mg every 8 hours. Severe: 875 mg every 12 hours or 500 mg every 8 hours. 6. Genitourinary System Infections: Mild/Moderate: 500 mg every 12 hours or 250 mg every 8 hours. Severe: 875 mg every 12 hours or 500 mg every 8 hours. 7. Lower Respiratory Tract Infections: 875 mg every 12 hours or 500 mg every 8 hours. 8. Tonsillitis and/or Pharyngitis: 775 mg once daily within 1 hour of finishing a meal for 10 days. Pediatric Indications and Dosage: 1. Otitis Media with Effusion: Mild/Moderate: 25 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 12 hours or 20 mg/kg/day every 8 hours. Severe: 45 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 12 hours or 40 mg/kg/day every 8 hours. 2. Acute Bacterial Rhinosinusitis: Mild/Moderate: 25 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 12 hours or 20 mg/kg/day every 8 hours. Severe: 45 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 12 hours or 40 mg/kg/day every 8 hours. 3. Gonorrhea (Uncomplicated Anogenital and Urethral Infections): 50 mg/kg amoxicillin combined with 25 mg/kg probenecid (for children >2 years old). 4. Skin and Subcutaneous Tissue Infections: Mild/Moderate: 25 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 12 hours or 20 mg/kg/day every 8 hours. Severe: 45 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 12 hours or 40 mg/kg/day every 8 hours. 5. Lower Respiratory Tract Infections: 45 mg/kg/day in divided doses every 12 hours or 40 mg/kg/day every 8 hours. 6. Tonsillitis and/or Pharyngitis: For children >12 years: 775 mg once daily within 1 hour of finishing a meal for 10 days. Contraindications: Amoxicillin is contraindicated in patients with a history of allergic reactions to penicillins. Warnings: 1. Hypersensitivity: Serious and sometimes fatal hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported. These are more common in individuals with a history of penicillin hypersensitivity or multiple allergen sensitivities. If an allergic reaction occurs, discontinue amoxicillin immediately and initiate appropriate therapy. Severe anaphylactic reactions require emergency treatment with epinephrine, oxygen, intravenous steroids, and airway management. 2. Clostridium difficile-Associated Diarrhea (CDAD): CDAD has been reported with nearly all antibacterial agents, including amoxicillin. It can range from mild diarrhea to fatal colitis. If CDAD is suspected, discontinue ongoing antibiotic use not directed against C. difficile and provide appropriate treatment. Adverse Reactions: 1. Gastrointestinal: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, black hairy tongue, and pseudomembranous colitis. 2. Hypersensitivity Reactions: Anaphylaxis, serum sickness-like reactions, erythematous maculopapular rashes, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, and urticaria. 3. Liver: Elevated AST/ALT, cholestatic jaundice, and acute cytolytic hepatitis. 4. Renal: Crystalluria. 5. Hemic and Lymphatic Systems: Anemia (including hemolytic anemia), thrombocytopenia, eosinophilia, and leukopenia. 6. Central Nervous System: Hyperactivity, agitation, anxiety, insomnia, confusion, and convulsions. 7. Miscellaneous: Tooth discoloration (brown, yellow, or gray staining). Use in Specific Populations: 1. Pregnancy: Category B (FDA): Animal studies have shown no harm to the fetus, but adequate studies in pregnant women are lacking. Use only if clearly needed. 2. Nursing Mothers: Amoxicillin is excreted in human milk and may sensitize infants. Use with caution. 3. Pediatric Use: Neonates and young infants may have delayed elimination due to immature renal function. Dosage adjustments are necessary for patients ≤3 months old. 4. Geriatric Use: No significant differences in response between elderly and younger patients. However, elderly patients are more likely to have decreased renal function, requiring careful dose selection and monitoring. Administration and Monitoring: Administer orally. During prolonged therapy, periodically assess renal, hepatic, and hematopoietic function. Patients with gonorrhea should undergo serologic testing for syphilis at diagnosis and follow-up testing after 3 months. Overdosage: In case of overdose, discontinue medication, treat symptomatically, and provide supportive measures. Amoxicillin can be removed by hemodialysis. Pharmacology: Amoxicillin inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis, leading to bacterial death. It is stable in gastric acid and rapidly absorbed after oral administration. Most of the drug is excreted unchanged in the urine. Storage: Store capsules, tablets, and unreconstituted powder at controlled room temperature (15°–30°C). Reconstituted suspension should be refrigerated and discarded after 14 days. Brand Names: Amoxil, Trimox, Wymox, Moxatag.
